subject: chemistry-1
question: A calcium atom has 20 protons. In calcium chloride, calcium is present as a particle containing 20 protons and 18 electrons. Which statement best describes how the bond in this compound forms?

options.text: Two atoms share a pair of valence electrons unequally, producing partial charges but no full ions.
Two atoms share one pair of valence electrons equally, so neither atom ends up carrying any charge.
One atom transfers valence electrons to another, and the resulting oppositely charged ions attract electrostatically.
Fixed metal cations are held in place by a sea of delocalized electrons shared among all the atoms.

explanation:
An ionic bond is the electrostatic attraction between a cation and an anion generated by electron transfer, typically from a metal of low ionization energy to a nonmetal of high electron affinity. A particle with 20 protons and 18 electrons carries a net charge of 20 - 18 = 2+, confirming that calcium has lost two electrons; each chlorine gains one, becoming Cl-. Option B describes a nonpolar covalent bond, option A a polar covalent bond, and option D metallic bonding, none of which involves the full charge separation seen here.

ELI-10: Charge is just a proton-versus-electron headcount. Calcium normally has 20 of each, so it is neutral. Hand two electrons away and it still has 20 protons but only 18 electrons, leaving it two positive units short of balanced: Ca2+. The chlorine atoms that caught those electrons each end up one unit negative. Opposite charges pull on each other, and that pull between transferred-electron ions is the ionic bond.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
